title: Ceva's Theorem: Non-Euclidean Extensions
openQuestion: How does the theorem extend to non-Euclidean geometries?

insights: All three geometries (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic) satisfy the same algebraic identity: ρ(BD)/ρ(DC) · ρ(CE)/ρ(EA) · ρ(AF)/ρ(FB) = 1 where ρ is id, sin, or sinh respectively
The generalized framework reduces all versions to: product of positive ratios = 1 iff numerator product = denominator product
Spherical Ceva uses sin of arc lengths (positive on (0,π)); hyperbolic Ceva uses sinh of distances (positive on (0,∞))
The trigonometric Ceva (sin of angles) is the Euclidean version but expressed via angle bisections rather than segment ratios
Flat limits connect all three: sin(x)/x → 1 and sinh(x)/x → 1 as x → 0, derived from derivatives at 0
HasDerivAt for sinh was built manually from exp derivatives since Real.hasDerivAt_sinh is not in Docker Mathlib v4.26.0
The unified principle theorem abstracts over any positive ratio function ρ

Specialization theorems for each geometry type
Special cases: medians in spherical and hyperbolic geometry
